messages:
nina: Heads up — we're seeing sustained queueing in the reserved pool rsv-eu-w-std (eu-west). Queue depth and admission_throttle count rising quickly. Notified here first.
ops-oncall: Ack, I'm looking at ingress graphs now.
sam: Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/POOL/rsv-eu-w-std — queue_len and admission_throttle look correlated, started ~10:42 UTC.
kevin: fairshare_evictions is spiking too. Looks like tenant acme-prod is consuming a disproportionate share after yesterday's rollout.
maya: Were there any long-running evals kicked off from the CI window last night?
sam: Searching logs, `kubectl logs -ljob=eval-runner -n reserved-eu | grep acme` shows a few >6h runs.
kevin: That matches. Those eval runs pinned a few GPUs and bumped their concurrent weights. Pool effective capacity dropped.
nina: Can we throttle the eval jobs first? Priority is customer SLAs for Dedicated tenants.
ops-oncall: I can evict the two oldest eval pods from the reserved namespace. Running:
```
kubectl delete pod eval-runner-7cf4 -n reserved-eu
kubectl delete pod eval-runner-9a2d -n reserved-eu
```
sam: Doing a quick query to confirm source of requests:
```
sum by(tenant) (rate(reserved_pool_inflight{pool="rsv-eu-w-std"}[1m]))
```
kevin: Query returns acme-prod ~45%, sandbox-team ~8%, others split. acme-prod ramp looks abnormal.
maya: acme-prod had a canary rollout yesterday morning that should have been batched. Pinged their infra lead.
ops-oncall: Evictions executed — pods terminated. Watching admission_throttle now.
sre-bot: Alert: reserved_pool_admission_throttle > 1000 in rsv-eu-w-std (automated paging)
sam: Throttle rate dropped ~30% after evictions, queue depth falling slowly.
kevin: We probably need a short-lived bias: reduce acme-prod weight to 0.6 and enable burst +1 GPU to avoid customer impact while we investigate.
ops-oncall: Proposed command to lower tenant weight:
```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/pools/rsv-eu-w-std/weights -d '{"tenant":"acme-prod","weight":0.6}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```
ops-oncall: And to add burst capacity +1 instance:
```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/pools/rsv-eu-w-std/scale -d '{"delta":1}'
```
nina: Do the weight change first, then scale if throttle still > baseline. Also prepare rollback steps.
maria: I'll draft a short status page blurb. We should note "degraded performance for dedicated reservations in eu-west; mitigation in progress" and link to incident.
kevin: Applying weight change now.
ops-oncall: Weight updated, scaling +1 requested. Backend accepted.
sam: Metrics: admission_throttle down 65% over 3m, queue_len back to baseline in most shards. Some tail latency spikes remain.
maya: acme infra says they launched a burst test accidentally. They've paused the tests and will open a support ticket.
nina: Good, keep monitoring for 20m, then we can revert weight and scale back down. Assigning follow-ups: acme-prod follow-up to sam, capacity audit to kevin.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4829 reserved-pool saturation — rsv-eu-w-std. Pager closed: mitigation applied.
maria: Status page posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-2026-4829 — short note + next update in 30m.
ops-oncall: 20m check-in: queue_len stable, admission_throttle within SLO. Will schedule a slow drain of the extra instance and restore weights to previous values.
kevin: Opening a postmortem stub and tagging product + infra. Root cause likely tenant-side test + missing local limits in our admission policy.
nina: Thanks all. Keep ticket updates in INC-2026-4829. If any regression, escalate to oncall immediately.
maria: Closing loop for customer comms — will reach out to affected enterprise contacts with summary and actions.
ops-oncall: Extra instance removed and weights restored at 11:18 UTC. Monitoring green.
sam: Final metrics snapshot: admission_throttle ~ baseline, p95 latency normal.
kevin: Postmortem owner assigned to kevin. Suggested action items: tenant weight guardrails, auto-detect runaway evals, guard for nightly CI windows.
nina: Resolved for now. Nice quick triage and good coordination. :thumbsup:"
